summary: Verified from the PDF Hodges arXiv:2311.07078 Thm 1.1 (G(n,q), fixed prime ℓ, n→∞: P((S_ℓ,δ)≅(G,δ_G)) = ∏_k(1−ℓ^{1−2k})/(|G||Aut(G,δ_G)|)); for G=ℤ/ℓ both pairing classes have |Aut|=2, so the CKLPW/Hodges model predicts square:non-square = 1:1 (Wood arXiv:1402.5149 does the groups only). Over all fan (hub+path) words p=tuv−u−v, t,u,v≥2, at primes p≤10⁷ (C, 8 s) the non-square pairing class ((tu−1)/p)=−1 has frequency 0.707 (p≡1 mod 8), 0.762 (p≡5 mod 8), 0.279/0.324 (p≡3/7 mod 8), slowly drifting toward 0.75 (aggregate 0.725→0.736 over decades 10³…10⁷). So the iid-1/2 prediction fails: CERTIFIED numbers, and the deviation is explained exactly by LOWERTAIL_ROUND2_FABLE.md Thm 1 (PROVED: '(uv/n) = −1 ⟺ {t,u,v}∩𝒞_n ≠ ∅'), i.e. the pairing class of a fan word is a deterministic 2-adic cell function (60 of 80 cells mod 8 for each p mod 8 = 0.75), not a random variable. Assessment: the sandpile Cohen–Lenstra/Hodges law is a large-random-graph theorem for fixed ℓ and does not model the 4-vertex fan family at ℓ=p; the correct heuristic for ES₅ is the 2-adic cell density 3/4 per word (iid-1/2 would predict Σ2^{−W}≈3.7 failures ≤10⁷ at p≡1(4); observed none besides p=5 with W=0).
not_done: Did not test random large graphs with τ=p (that is just Hodges' theorem); did not include boundary words with an entry 1; did not read CKLPW 2015 itself (Hodges Lemma 10.1 quotes its Thm 2).
next: None for the CL route; any random model for ES₅ should use the 2-adic cell density (LOWERTAIL_ROUND2_FABLE Thm 1), not pairing coin flips.

summary: Implemented the GPPV/CCFGH homological blocks (arXiv:1809.10148 eq. (6.2)/(6.4)–(6.5): v.p. constant-term formula over ℓ∈2Mℤ^L+b) for star plumbings, calibrated exactly against CCFGH (6.12)–(6.13) for M(−1;1/2,1/3,1/9) and against Σ(2,3,5) = q^{−3/2}(1−q−q³−q⁷+q⁸+q¹⁴+q²⁰+q²⁹−q³¹−q⁴²…), then computed the Weyl-symmetrised δ-block for all 373 ES Seifert spaces M(−3;(x−1)/x,(y−1)/y,(z−1)/z) (e=−4/n, |H₁|=xy+yz+zx verified) with 5≤n≤25, z≤3000. PROVED (direct computation, checked on all 373): M⁻¹ on {centre, leg ends} is B_cc=1/e, B_ci=1/(e a_i), B_ij=1/(e a_i a_j)−δ_ij(a_i−1)/a_i, so each block is a sum of ≤8 false thetas Σ±½ sgn(ℓ) q^{(n/16)(ℓ+Σε_i/a_i)²}, ℓ in one residue class mod 2·ord(e_c), and Ẑ_δ = q^{(n−8)/16 − (x+y+z−6)/4}(1 − q + O(q^g)) with g between 10 and 7.9·10⁶ (very lacunary). The only n-only ingredients are the Euler number and the ε=±(1,1,1) exponents (nℓ±4)²/(16n), which is just the ES equation restated; everything else (Δ via x+y+z, ord(e_c), gaps, block classes) varies with the solution, and a sum over solutions of the leading terms is only a perimeter generating function Σ q^{−(x+y+z)/4}. No n-level structure beyond the equation was seen.
not_done: Only the δ-block (and its Weyl partner), not all |H₁| blocks or the WRT/radial-limit combination; no quantum-modularity (Weil representation m+K) identification; n≤25 only (z≤3000).
next: None unless a theory predicts an n-only combination of blocks; the solution-dependence is generic.

summary:
Premise check: the stated facts hold (Riemenschneider: the dual of [[v,t,u]] has length v+t+u−5; (p−A/p)=(A/p) at p≡1 (4)), and the point diagram gives the exact dual shape p/(p−A) = [[2^{v−2},3,2^{t−3},3,2^{u−2}]] (or [[2^{v−2},4,2^{u−2}]] if t=2), so ES₅(p) ⟺ some QNR B has p/B of this shape (PROVED, elementary). C brute force over all B

1000), the opposite of the Zaremba regime (all digits ≤ 5; cf. FRONTIER §3 Zaremba remark). The dual picture is a class-preserving relabelling A↦p−A and adds no counting tool.
not_done: No attempt at a digit-structure counting theorem (none applies: certificates need one digit ≥ p^{1/3}−2); brute force stopped at 3·10⁵ (quadratic cost).
next: None; the dual form is equivalent to ES₅ and lies outside bounded-digit methods.

summary: The natural quadric is already in the repo: words ↔ γ_w = [[A,n],[t,A*]] = (HJ product M(u)M(t)M(v) up to signs) on AA* − tn = 1 (signature (2,2); its SO(2,1)/adjoint image gives the (2,1) form), QUESTION_R.md Prop 1.1, which notes the gap 'these sets are not semigroup orbits'. I did the missing orbit test. PROVED (elementary): if g ∈ SL₂(ℤ) satisfies gW₃ ⊆ W₃ (W₃ = all length-3 word matrices), then g = T^k, k ≥ 0. Proof: for g = [[α,β],[γ,δ]] with γ ≠ 0, letting u → ∞ at fixed t, a′+1 = t(αu+β)−α+1 ≡ 0 mod c′ = t(γu+δ)−γ forces α = kγ and t(β−kδ)+1 = 0, impossible for t ≥ 2. CERTIFIED: among all 116² pairs (g,h) ∈ SL₂(ℤ)² with entries ≤ 3, tested on the 343 words with t,u,v ≤ 8, exactly the 32 pairs ±(T^a, T^b), 0 ≤ a,b ≤ 3, satisfy gW₃h ⊆ W₃ (these are u ↦ u+a, v ↦ v+b). So W₃ = ⊔_t T^ℕ γ_{(t,2,2)} T^ℕ is a union of parabolic (abelian, non-Zariski-dense) double orbits, one per level t, and no thin Zariski-dense group acts on the ES₅ word data in this quadric; an Apollonian/HKRS-type orbit would need a different encoding, and none was found.
evidence: BRAINSTORM/apollonian_reciprocity.md §3 (no Vieta involution at fixed n)
not_done: No search over arbitrary (non-equivariant) encodings into other quadrics, and no SL₂(ℤ[i]) (signature (3,1), Bianchi) stabiliser test; the two-sided stabiliser was only certified in the box |entries| ≤ 3 (left-sided: proved).
next: None; any thin-orbit model must change the encoding, since the word set has only parabolic symmetries.

summary: Read CHJ arXiv:1909.02332 (§4: cutting any subpolygon out of a triangulated polygon gives a frieze with coefficients; Lemma 4.2 gcd condition; Lemma 4.4 Euclid construction; Thm 1.1 = Thm 5.12: (a,b,c) is a cut-out triangle iff the pairwise gcds agree and ν₂ all 0 or not all equal; §6 finiteness). Since c_{ij}=1 iff ij is an edge/arc and arcs separate, a pentagon with boundary (1,1,1,1,N) cut out of a CC frieze is exactly five consecutive vertices V1..V5 of a triangulated polygon, and c_{V1V3},c_{V2V4},c_{V3V5} are the triangle counts at V2,V3,V4; so a word (c,m,s) ⟺ three consecutive vertices with c, m, s triangles and N = c_{V1V5} = cms−c−s (PROVED, continuant identity); the rest of the triangulation is free. Explicit fan+ear construction realises all 1 999 words (incl. boundary words) of all primes N≡1 (4) < 600 (0 failures, quiddity product −I checked); the sign (h′/N)=−1 ⟺ a triangle count at V2,V3,V4 lies in 𝒞_N = 4ℤ∪(8ℤ−N) ⟺ 4 | one of the five diagonals (0 mismatches; this is LOWERTAIL_ROUND2_FABLE Thm 1 / FRIEZE_ES Cor 1.3), and CHJ's 2-adic triangle condition is vacuous here because every sub-triangle of the pentagon contains a side 1 or N (0 violations). So the sign is 'visible' only as triangle counts mod 8 at the three middle vertices, which is the known coordinate form; the CHJ cut-out model adds no new invariant.
not_done: Did not study CHJ §6 finiteness bounds for boundary (1,1,1,1,N) beyond noting the word set is finite (already known); no minimal-polygon-size statistics.
next: None; the cut-out picture is the coordinate form in triangulation language.

summary: From QUATERNION_ES Lemma 1.1, α = 1+2aw lies in the primitive ideal 𝔈 = [e, k+w], k ≡ (2a)⁻¹ (mod e), of norm e (form (e,2k,(k²+d)/e), disc −4d), with 1+2bw ∈ 𝔈̄ and 𝔈·(α/𝔈) principal. PROVED: since pe = 4abd−1 ≡ −1 (mod 4d), every assigned genus character of disc −4d satisfies χ(𝔈) = χ(−p), so the genus of 𝔈 is forced by p alone (the genus of −p; principal genus iff all χ(−p)=1, e.g. whenever e = 1). Computation (own Gauss composition, Cohen Alg 5.4.7, class numbers checked on d=5…89): all 1 645 455 Type I solutions with p ≤ 10⁵, d ≤ 200: 0 genus failures; beyond genus nothing is forced — for e>1 (1 354 284 solutions) [𝔈] is principal 827 521 times vs 803 792 expected under 'uniform over the norm-e ideals in the forced genus', mean class order 2.09 vs 2.12, orders up to 20 occur, and the order histogram tracks the uniform-in-genus model (e.g. ord 3: 80 779 vs 112 603; ord 6: 48 918 vs 41 919), deviations being small-e/small-a size effects. So the 'class of order ≤ 2·something' hope fails; the forced layer is exactly genus = the quadratic-character layer.
not_done: No Heegner/CM equidistribution input was attempted (the item's 'native next step'); classes computed for the order ℤ[√−d] (non-maximal when d ≡ 3 mod 4 or d non-squarefree) only; d ≤ 200, p ≤ 10⁵.
next: None: the forced information is the genus (= BM/quadratic layer); the class inside the genus behaves like the uniform model.

summary: Complete searches (scripts/z52_bank_pencil.c, odd n ≤ 5·10⁴): non-square fibres have only sporadic zeros (k=2: 13 zeros, k=3: only n=13, k=5: 21, 57, k=6: none, k=7: 9 zeros ≤ 10⁴, none in (10⁴, 5·10⁴)), against 1262/1250/417 zeros at square controls k=1/4/9 for odd n < 10⁴. The unique k=3 zero n=13 is the unique point on the Mordell locus 4k+n³=□ (13³+12=47²), where Z52_BANKED §1(a) says 𝒜=(−q,−d) is unramified; all 133 901 integral-place local symbols at (13,3) are +1. New Theorem 1(b) (PROVED here, Hilbert reciprocity via dd′=(ny+2k/n)²−k(s/n)²): if k=(s²−n³)/4 ≥ 1, gcd(n,k)=1 and (−n/ℓ)=1 for all ℓ | s, ℓ ∤ k, then S_{n,k}(ℕ)=∅. CERTIFIED on 55 861 Mordell pairs (n ≤ 3001, k ≤ 10⁶): 13 682/13 682 empty; with gcd=1 but a bad prime ℓ | s, (−n/ℓ)=−1, 57 % (17 829/31 548) are still empty vs 2.5 % (298/11 986) for adjacent non-Mordell controls. Assessment: the pencil obstruction lives on {k=□} ∪ {4k+n³=□}; for fixed non-square k the second set is finite (Siegel), and at k=0 it is exactly the odd squares, so T1 is the k→0 limit of the Mordell-locus obstruction (data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/parts/md_S4.md §Z2835).
not_done: Full Br S_{n,k}/Br ℚ not computed (no other classes searched for at the sporadic zeros, e.g. k=2, n=3465); the 57 % residual emptiness on bad-prime Mordell fibres is not explained (a quantitative strong-approximation effect is suspected); Thm 1(b) has had no independent review.
next: Independent review of Thm 1(b); then test whether the residual Mordell-fibre emptiness is a BM obstruction to strong approximation (solutions need a bad ℓ | d with y ≡ −2k/n² mod ℓ).
